title: The camera you play through
summary: The view in Supermarket Simulator is a system of its own: the game keeps a camera controller and presets, offers a free camera for looking around, invokes camera settings and listens for changes, and fits the picture to the screen.
body: The view is managed rather than fixed. The game keeps a camera controller of its own, which is why what you are looking at can change without the shop changing with it.
Setups can be kept. There are camera presets, so a particular way of looking at something is a thing the game can hold rather than something rebuilt each time.
There is a camera that is free of a body. The game has a free camera of its own, which is how the view can be taken somewhere a player is not.
Settings are announced rather than applied silently. Camera settings are invoked and listened for, so a change to the view can be made in one place and reacted to in another.
The picture is fitted to the screen. There is a fitter for the aspect ratio, which is why the same view works on a wide screen and a narrow one rather than being cropped.
The camera also carries settings you can change: the entry on the settings menu keeps its own camera settings and a listener that reacts to how wide the view is.
The camera knows what it is doing. It keeps a state of its own, which is how the game can tell one way of viewing from another without rebuilding the controller.
What this entry does not tell you: what each preset frames, how fast a camera moves, or how the aspect fitter chooses its cropping. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The view is run by a camera controller of its own.
Camera setups can be kept as presets.
There is a free camera of its own, separate from the one the player carries.
Camera settings are invoked and listened for rather than applied in one place.
The picture is fitted to the screen by a fitter of its own.
The camera has settings on the settings menu, with a listener that reacts to the field of view.
The camera also keeps a state of its own.
